newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch seek arrest of former Surinam military ruler.
newsitem.headline: Dutch seek arrest of former Surinam military ruler.

text.p: The Netherlands said on Wednesday it was seeking international cooperation to arrest Surinam's former military ruler Desi Bouterse as part of an investigation into his alleged involvement in drug smuggling.
Justice Ministry spokesman Victor Holtus said the Netherlands had filed a request to that effect with the international police organisation Interpol.
"The Dutch justice authorities have requested Bouterse's arrest with a view to his extradition to the Netherlands," he told Reuters.
Holtus said the move was linked to an ongoing criminal investigation into allegations that Bouterse was involved in large-scale cocaine smuggling operations.
The head of the Dutch public prosecution service said earlier this year that he expected to complete the investigation and bring charges against Bouterse within a year.
Bouterse led military coups in Surinam, a former Dutch colony in South America, in 1980 and 1990.

Officially, he does not hold public office in Surinam but his National Democratic Party (NDP) has led a five-party coalition government since elections last year and he was later appointed as an adviser to president Jules Wijdenbosch.
Few observers doubt that he is really controlling government policy from behind the scenes.
Bouterse has long been distrusted by the Netherlands where he is held responsible by many for ordering the summary execution in 1982 of 15 opposition leaders.

Allegations of Bouterse's involvement in drug-smuggling have surfaced periodically in the Dutch press, but it is only recently that Dutch authorities have confirmed that they were pursuing a criminal investigation against him.
In 1986 a Bouterse aide, Lieutenant Etienne Boerenveen, was given a jail sentence by a U.S. court for conspiracy to smuggle cocaine after being arrested by American agents posing as drug dealers.
